rules: Verification rule of the Depth datum plan (2026-11-22) section 3: a side is VERIFIED only when two independent publishers name the same datum for the same series or pool (or the datum is stamped by the series' own parameter definition AND an empirical cross-gauge check passes); a conversion is enabled only when the offset agrees with NOAA VDatum at the gauge within 0.10 ft; datum-name disagreement or offsets more than 0.25 ft apart is CONFLICT; at most two research passes per lake. Consumed by depth_research.candidates (verified_conversion); nothing here is read at runtime.
reviewer: claude-code (research pass; promotion into a knowledge release is Michael's decision)
evidenceNote: Evidence was read with a web fetcher that returns a model summary of the page, so `quote` is the value as reported by that fetch, not a byte-exact excerpt, and `sha256` is null (raw bytes were not retained). VDatum calls: /vdatumweb/api/convert, NAD27 geographic in, NGVD29 -> NAVD88, us_ft, region contiguous, geoid18.

empirical.method: Negreet 62615 (NAVD88) minus Burkeville 62614 (NGVD29), same 15-min timestamp, 9 dates 2025-12-15..2026-11-10
empirical.note: after the -0.2 ft conversion the two gauges agree within 0.3 ft on every sampled date (largest residual 0.15 ft); a mislabelled NGVD29 series would centre near 0, the NAVD88 label centres near -0.2

sameRecord.ownerDecision: Use the CWMS JPHT1 seasonal level (490.5 ft) as the reference so pool and level are same-source. Michael, chat 2026-11-22 07:14Z ("Yes 1-3"), recorded on Sector_Ops #51 and PR #223 comment
sameRecord.caveat: 490.5 ft is the summer value of a seasonal CWMS level (winter 483 ft); the reference stays a single constant like every other lake, so winter readings show the planned drawdown as a negative shift.
